name: RASA1-related capillary malformation-arteriovenous malformation

criteria.description: Presence of multiple small, round to oval, pink to red capillary malformations often with a pale halo
Identification of fast-flow arteriovenous malformations or fistulas by imaging or clinical examination
Detection of a pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant in the RASA1 gene
Family history of similar capillary malformations or AVMs consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic capillary malformations plus either confirmed AVM or pathogenic RASA1 variant
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is critical for confirmation; imaging is essential to identify AVMs.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multiple small round to oval capillary malformations with pale halos
searchTerms: multiple small red skin spots with pale rings
tiny round capillary marks with halos
small vascular skin lesions with light edges

common.symptomName: Localized soft tissue overgrowth adjacent to vascular malformations
searchTerms: localized tissue overgrowth near blood vessel malformations
soft tissue swelling adjacent to vascular lesions

common.symptomName: Recurrent bleeding or ulceration over vascular lesions
searchTerms: ulcers forming on blood vessel malformations

common.symptomName: Pulsatile bruit or thrill over AVM sites
Neurological symptoms secondary to cerebral AVMs (e.g., seizures, headaches)
searchTerms: neurological problems from brain vessel abnormalities

occasional.symptomName: High-output cardiac failure due to large AVMs
searchTerms: heart failure from high blood flow
high-output cardiac failure due to AVMs
one limb larger than the other

occasional.symptomName: Pain or discomfort at AVM sites
Nasal or oral mucosal vascular malformations
searchTerms: nose or mouth blood vessel malformations
abnormal blood vessels in nasal or oral mucosa
vascular birthmarks inside nose or mouth
brain bleed caused by vascular lesion
spinal blood vessel abnormalities causing spinal cord damage
abnormal spinal artery-vein connections causing nerve problems
spinal arteriovenous malformations with spinal cord symptoms

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; possible anemia if bleeding occurs
imaging: Doppler ultrasound showing fast-flow vascular malformations
MRI/MRA or CT angiography demonstrating AVMs and fistulas
Conventional angiography for detailed vascular mapping
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic capillary malformations with pale halos
Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Facial port-wine stain in trigeminal nerve distribution
Neurological deficits and seizures from birth

redFlags: Neurological deficits suggestive of cerebral AVM hemorrhage
references: Eerola I, Boon LM, Mulliken JB, et al. Capillary malformation-arteriovenous malformation, a new clinical and genetic disorder caused by RASA1 mutations. Am J Hum Genet. 2003;73(6):1240-1249.
